# Classical Latin, nominative singular and plural. English marks case by word

# The etymon column is the English word descended from the Latin one, usually a
# learned borrowing. For Latin this is the whole point: the reader is not
# memorising a foreign word, they are being shown where their own word came
# from. "vaccine" from vacca, cow. "mile" from mīlle passūs. "peninsula" from
# So an etymon is a published claim, and it is held to a dictionary. The
# English word must have come from this Latin word, or from one built on it:
# a word built on the same root beside it is a cousin, and is not claimed —
# "ludicrous" is from "lūdere", not "lūdus". Every etymon names the entry it
# was checked against in tools/seed/la-etymons.tsv, and
# tests/tools/etymons.test.ts fails on one that names none.
# IPA is generated from the orthography, which is very nearly deterministic

# The note column is a published sentence, so it is held to a dictionary.
